ActivityGraph.description:
A workflow's steps and the flow between them. `entry` is where the
InitialNode leads.
ActivityGraph.title: ActivityGraph

ActivityNode.description:
One step of a workflow. The field it references depends on its kind:
`tool`, `agent` or `workflow`.
ActivityNode.title: ActivityNode

ActivityNodeKind.description: A workflow step, as the UML ActivityNode it is (ADR-0102).
ActivityNodeKind.title: ActivityNodeKind

AgentEndpoint.description:
An agent outside this system that ours may call (ADR-0030).

The agentic workforce reaches past one organization. An endpoint is a
declared, trust-classified boundary: what it offers, what we may send it,
and what its answers are worth.
AgentEndpoint.title: AgentEndpoint

AgentMemoryOverride.description: An agent's narrowing of the system memory contract.
AgentMemoryOverride.title: AgentMemoryOverride

AgentSpec.description: One agent: who it answers to, what it is for, what it may reach.
AgentSpec.title: AgentSpec

ArtifactStore.description:
A workspace agents read and write files in (ADR-0036).

Distinct from memory (what an agent *learned*) and from a sandbox (where it
*executes*): this is where large intermediate material lives so it does not
have to sit in the context window.
ArtifactStore.title: ArtifactStore

AutonomyPosture.description:
How much of an activity an agent does without a person (ADR-0072).

Until this existed the posture was *emergent*: it fell out of the action,
whether the capability named a decision class, whether the agent held it,
and whether approval was required. Four independent fields, no stated
intent — so an activity could change from supervised to autonomous by
deleting one line and nothing could say that it had.
AutonomyPosture.title: AutonomyPosture

BindingDocument.description: A binding document: one or more target bindings for a spec.
BindingDocument.title: Binding

Budget.description: A spend ceiling with a mandatory action on breach (ADR-0022).
Budget.title: Budget

Cadence.description:
When a schedule fires, in a form both humans and targets can read.

`expression` is a five-field cron expression or a plain-English interval
("every 15 minutes", "every 2 hours"). Neither names a scheduler product.
Cadence.title: Cadence

Capability.description: An abstract access need, bound to an MCP server per target (ADR-0010).
Capability.title: Capability

CapabilityBinding.description:
How an abstract capability becomes a concrete MCP server mount.

Two forms: inline (name the connection here) or by reference (`server`
names a `ServerBinding` in the target's catalog, and the connection is
inherited; any field set here still overrides it). `server_name` is
optional when `server` is given — the catalog supplies it (ADR-0085).
CapabilityBinding.title: CapabilityBinding

CapabilityConstraint.description: Limits enforced at the capability boundary, never by the model.
CapabilityConstraint.title: CapabilityConstraint

CatchUpPolicy.description: What to do about runs missed while the system was down.
CatchUpPolicy.title: CatchUpPolicy

ChannelBinding.description:
How an abstract channel becomes a real surface people watch.

`provider` is where implementation names are allowed: slack, msteams, smtp,
a ticketing system. `bot_identity_ref` is a reference to the workspace
identity the agent posts as — a name, never a token (ADR-0015).
ChannelBinding.title: ChannelBinding

ChannelClass.description: Abstract communication surfaces; the binding picks the product.
ChannelClass.title: ChannelClass

ChannelPurpose.description: Why an agent contacts a human on a channel (ADR-0021).
ChannelPurpose.title: ChannelPurpose

ChannelSpec.description:
A communication surface, abstract in the spec and bound per target.

Human-facing channels carry a contract (ADR-0021): what they are for, when
the people on them are available, how fast a reply is expected, and who is
tried next when it does not come.
ChannelSpec.title: ChannelSpec

Compliance.description: Obligations that constrain placement, retention and disclosure.
Compliance.title: Compliance

ContextPolicy.description: How a long run keeps its context usable and affordable (ADR-0036).
ContextPolicy.title: ContextPolicy

ControlEnforcement.description: Who enforces this control, and what we are trusting them for.
ControlEnforcement.title: ControlEnforcement

ControlEnforcer.description:
Who actually enforces a control (ADR-0073).

An agentic organization does not replace its enterprise applications. The
ERP owns the ledger, the treasury system owns the sweep, the bank owns the
payment, and each carries its own controls. A spec that describes a bound
without saying who checks it reads as governed when it may not be.
ControlEnforcer.title: ControlEnforcer

ControlFlow.description: An edge between two steps; `END` is the ActivityFinalNode.
ControlFlow.title: ControlFlow

DataClass.description: A classification that drives access, placement and egress (ADR-0017).
DataClass.title: DataClass

DataDependency.description:
What an agent relies on about data it reads (ADR-0099).

Not a schema. A schema belongs to whoever owns the data; restating it here
would be a copy that is correct until their next migration. This is the
*consumer's* half of a contract: which class, which fields of it, how
fresh, from whom, and what to do when the promise does not hold.
DataDependency.title: DataDependency

DataRelation.description: One edge between two data classes.
DataRelation.title: DataRelation

DataRelationKind.description:
How one class of data relates to another.

Each kind exists because something checks it. A relation nothing reads is
decoration, which is the bar every relationship in this platform has to
clear (ADR-0081).
DataRelationKind.title: DataRelationKind

DataSemantics.description:
What a class of data *is*, as distinct from how it is protected.

Deliberately five, and deliberately coarse. The point is not to describe a
schema — the system that owns the data does that — but to carry enough
meaning for a rule to follow (ADR-0099).
DataSemantics.title: DataSemantics

DecisionClass.description:
A class of decision a unit may be authorized to take (ADR-0065).

Declared in the spec, like a capability, so a mandate references a term
somebody wrote down rather than inventing one per team. `ADR-0066` holds
the open question of whether these should eventually be catalog-owned.
DecisionClass.title: DecisionClass

DeploymentSpec.description: Which targets this system compiles for; bindings live separately.
DeploymentSpec.title: DeploymentSpec

EndpointTrust.description: How far an external agent endpoint is trusted (ADR-0030).
EndpointTrust.title: EndpointTrust

EnvironmentBinding.description: How an abstract environment class becomes a concrete workspace.
EnvironmentBinding.title: EnvironmentBinding

EnvironmentOverride.description: An agent's narrowing of its environment class. Widening is rejected.
EnvironmentOverride.title: EnvironmentOverride

EscalationStep.description: Who to try next when nobody answers, and when.
EscalationStep.title: EscalationStep

EvaluationCase.description: One check an agent must pass before it may be promoted (ADR-0022).
EvaluationCase.title: EvaluationCase

FailurePolicy.description: What happens when a triggered run fails (ADR-0020).
FailurePolicy.title: FailurePolicy

FlowKind.description: A declared directional interaction between agents (ADR-0024).
FlowKind.title: FlowKind

GateRequirement.description: What must be true before an agent advances a stage (ADR-0022).
GateRequirement.title: GateRequirement

Guardrail.description:
A boundary check on what enters or leaves an agent (ADR-0035).

Permissions decide what an agent may *reach*; a guardrail decides what may
*pass*. They are different questions, and a system that answers only the
first will happily let a correctly-permissioned agent paste a customer's
identifiers into a chat channel.
Guardrail.title: Guardrail

GuardrailAction.description: What happens when a check trips.
GuardrailAction.title: GuardrailAction

GuardrailCheck.description: Named checks, so a guardrail is reviewable rather than a regex soup.
GuardrailCheck.title: GuardrailCheck

GuardrailKind.description: Where a guardrail sits in the loop (ADR-0035).
GuardrailKind.title: GuardrailKind

HumanCounterpart.description:
A person paired with an agent, in a named capacity (ADR-0026).

An agent has one `owner` and may have any number of approvers, reviewers,
escalation contacts, operators and stakeholders. Pairing is many-to-many:
one person can be the owner of several agents and a reviewer on others.
HumanCounterpart.title: HumanCounterpart

HumanRole.description:
Why a person is paired with an agent (ADR-0026).

An agent answers to several people in different capacities: one is
accountable for it, others approve specific actions, review its output, or
are simply told what it did.
HumanRole.title: HumanRole

InfrastructureBinding.description: Provider-side choices for the neutral resource set (ADR-0012).
InfrastructureBinding.title: InfrastructureBinding

InteractionFlow.description:
A declared directional edge between agents (ADR-0024).

The org tree already implies delegation down a hierarchy. Flows express
what the tree cannot: that an analyst may *consult* compliance without
being able to instruct it, and that the reverse does not hold.
InteractionFlow.title: InteractionFlow

KnowledgeBinding.description: Which concrete system backs a declared grounding source (ADR-0023).
KnowledgeBinding.title: KnowledgeBinding

KnowledgeKind.description: Classes of grounding source, not products (ADR-0023).
KnowledgeKind.title: KnowledgeKind

KnowledgeSource.description: Grounding material an agent may consult (ADR-0023).
KnowledgeSource.title: KnowledgeSource

Lifecycle.description: Stages, gates and the review cadence for the whole system (ADR-0022).
Lifecycle.title: Lifecycle

Mandate.description:
A bounded scope of decision held by a unit (ADR-0065).

Not a description of work — that is a responsibility. This is what the
unit may settle without asking: permission decides whether the door
opens, a mandate decides whether you were the one to open it.
Mandate.title: Mandate

Memory.description: The two-tier memory contract for the system (ADR-0028).
Memory.title: Memory

MemoryBinding.description: Where the two memory tiers actually live (ADR-0028).
MemoryBinding.title: MemoryBinding

MemoryNamespace.description: A partition of long-term memory, scoped like any other data.
MemoryNamespace.title: MemoryNamespace

Mission.description:
A short-lived team drawn from the standing organization (ADR-0039).

The org chart changes slowly and describes accountability. A mission
changes weekly and describes *work*: a named objective, deliverables, a
leader, the people on it, and a date it ends. Members keep their home team
and their own permissions; the mission is a temporary working arrangement,
not a reorganization.
Mission.title: Mission

MissionStatus.description: Where a short-lived team is in its life (ADR-0039).
MissionStatus.title: MissionStatus

ModelBinding.description: Which model serves an agent loop.
ModelBinding.title: ModelBinding

ModelClass.title: ModelClass

ModelPolicy.description:
Which models an agent is permitted to run on (ADR-0040).

Stated as capability classes plus constraints, so the design stays neutral;
the catalog resolves classes to concrete models and the compiler refuses a
binding that picks one outside this policy.
ModelPolicy.title: ModelPolicy

Observability.description: The contract every target must satisfy (ADR-0016).
Observability.title: Observability

Organization.description:
The root of one organisation, and the owner of everything in it
(ADR-0101).

A Team by generalisation — it has a leader, members and sub-teams like any
unit — and the one unit that is *the organisation*: exactly one per
system, no parent, and it always declares placement (ADR-0069). Every
element of the organisation's model is composed here: its people, roles,
capabilities, data classes, environments, skills, knowledge, workflows and
the links between its units and agents. What stays on the System is how
the design is run and released, not what the organisation is.

`role_definitions` rather than `roles`: a Team's `roles` are the role
*assignments* the unit holds, which the organisation inherits as a team.
Organization.title: Organization

OutputContract.description:
The shape an agent, sub-agent or tool must return (ADR-0037).

`returns: "a cited findings list"` tells a person what to expect and tells
a caller nothing it can check. A contract is checkable.
OutputContract.title: OutputContract

OverlapPolicy.description: What to do when a run is still going and the next one is due.
OverlapPolicy.title: OverlapPolicy

Person.description:
A named human, declared once, as a principal for authority (ADR-0079).

A person holds a **mandate** and never a capability or a permission. We do
not mediate a person's access — they sign into the ERP under their
employer's IAM — and a permission this platform cannot enforce is worse
than none (the rule ADR-0073 applies to controls, applied to principals).

`capabilities` and `permissions` exist here only so the validator can
refuse them with that reason. They are read by
`validate_spec`'s `person_holds_access` check and by nothing else; a
pydantic error would refuse the spec without explaining why.

What is declared here is a **claim**. The person's real delegation of
authority lives in their employer's approval matrix, which this platform
does not read and nothing reconciles. We declare it because this platform
is what routes the escalation.
Person.title: Person

PluginSpec.description: An installable bundle of skills and tools (ADR-0029).
PluginSpec.title: PluginSpec

PolicyRule.description: An explicit allow or deny; deny always wins and cannot be overridden.
PolicyRule.title: PolicyRule

PromotionGate.description: What must hold before an agent enters a stage (ADR-0022).
PromotionGate.title: PromotionGate

ProtocolBinding.description:
Which wire protocol an external agent endpoint is reached over.

The spec says an endpoint exists, what it is trusted as and what may be
sent to it; *which protocol* reaches it is an implementation choice and
lives here, like a model provider or a channel (ADR-0002, ADR-0058).
Protocol names are the runtime registry's vocabulary and are deliberately
not enumerated in this module — the same stance `WorkflowBinding` takes
towards engine names.
ProtocolBinding.title: ProtocolBinding

Resilience.description: Durability properties a target must provide (ADR-0025).
Resilience.title: Resilience

ResourceKind.description: Kinds of resource a permission or capability can address.
ResourceKind.title: ResourceKind

ResourceTier.description: Abstract size of an execution environment.
ResourceTier.title: ResourceTier

Role.description: Responsibilities, capabilities and permissions as one contract (ADR-0007).
Role.title: Role

anyOf.description: A role bound to an agent or team; may narrow, never widen.
anyOf.title: RoleAssignment

RuntimeBinding.description: Which agent framework executes the loop (ADR-0013).
RuntimeBinding.title: RuntimeBinding

RuntimeRequirement.description: What the agent loop must support — not which framework provides it.
RuntimeRequirement.title: RuntimeRequirement

ScalingPolicy.description:
How many of this agent run, and how much each one takes on (ADR-0095).

Vendor-neutral on purpose: these are statements about expected load and
tolerated latency, which are facts about the organization's work rather
than about whichever cloud was chosen to run it. A binding that changed
them would mean two deployments of one design disagreed about how much
work an agent does.

Scale-to-zero is not a field here. It is `min_instances == 0`, because a
flag that could disagree with the number beside it is a bug waiting to
happen. What it costs is real and stated where it is chosen: an agent at
zero loses the process holding its asynchronous handles (ADR-0093) and any
standing-in it was doing (ADR-0094).
ScalingPolicy.title: ScalingPolicy

ScheduleBinding.description: Which scheduler actually fires the triggers (ADR-0020).
ScheduleBinding.title: ScheduleBinding

SeparationRule.description:
Decisions no single principal may hold together (ADR-0070).

Hierarchical narrowing and separation of duties pull in opposite
directions: narrowing requires every parent to hold at least the union of
its children, while separation requires that *no one principal* holds both
sides of a control. Both cannot govern the same objects, so a team is a
scope and this constrains agents.
SeparationRule.title: SeparationRule

ServerBinding.description:
A backing enterprise system, declared once and shared by capabilities.

An enterprise has a handful of systems — an ERP, a data warehouse, an
order-management system, a document store — and dozens of capabilities that
reach into them. Declaring the connection on every capability repeats the
system's URL, credential and trust posture N times and hides the fact that
twenty capabilities all land on one server. A server catalog names each
system once; a capability then references it by `server` and inherits the
connection (ADR-0085). It is also the deployment's systems inventory — the
thing an auditor asks for.
ServerBinding.title: ServerBinding

SharingScope.description: How widely a data class may travel.
SharingScope.title: SharingScope

SkillSpec.description:
A packaged capability pack an agent can hold (ADR-0029).

A skill is instructions plus optional resources — it changes how an agent
works, not what it may reach. Access always comes from capabilities.
SkillSpec.title: SkillSpec

StaleAction.description:
What to do when data is older than the agent said it could rely on.

Staleness is a state, not a crash. `REFUSE` is the default because a
freshness window that carried on regardless would be decorative, and this
platform does not ship a control that reads as enforced and is not
(ADR-0073).
StaleAction.title: StaleAction

SubAgentKind.description: What a tool-shaped sub-agent is for (ADR-0027).
SubAgentKind.title: SubAgentKind

SubAgentSpec.description:
A task-scoped worker an agent calls like a tool (ADR-0027).

A sub-agent is not an org member: it has no reporting line, no human
counterpart of its own, no session URL and no memory beyond the call. It
runs under its parent's identity with a **narrowed** set of that parent's
capabilities, returns a result, and is gone.
SubAgentSpec.title: SubAgentSpec

TargetBinding.description: Everything one target needs beyond the spec.
TargetBinding.title: TargetBinding

Team.description: A team with exactly one leader, members, and nested child teams (ADR-0006).
Team.title: Team

ToolSpec.description:
A named callable an agent sees, wrapping something else (ADR-0029).

A tool is a thin, reviewable wrapper: it narrows and names an underlying
capability, sub-agent, workflow or external endpoint. It never grants
anything its target does not already grant.
ToolSpec.title: ToolSpec

ToolchainClass.description: Categories of tooling an environment may need, not concrete images.
ToolchainClass.title: ToolchainClass

TriggerSpec.description:
Something that starts a run without a person asking (ADR-0020).

A triggered run carries exactly the same permission envelope as interactive
work: it is the agent's own capabilities and identity, never a separate
service account with broader reach.
TriggerSpec.title: TriggerSpec

UnitLink.description:
An association between two units that is not containment (ADR-0081).

Containment is `team.teams`: one parent, authority narrows through it,
placement inherits through it. This is everything else — the relationships
a real organisation has that a tree cannot hold. It grants nothing,
narrows nothing and inherits nothing.
UnitLink.title: UnitLink

UnitLinkKind.description:
How two units are related when one does not contain the other.

Every kind carries a consequence, because a relationship with none is
decoration (ADR-0081). `PARTNERS_WITH` is the exception and says so: it is
declared inert, because the alternative is people expressing an inert
relationship as an `OVERSEES` that is not one.
UnitLinkKind.title: UnitLinkKind

WorkflowBinding.description:
Which engine runs a declared workflow, and how it is reached (ADR-0056).

The spec says what a workflow is for; this says what executes it. Engine
names are deliberately *not* enumerated here — the runtime registry owns
that vocabulary, the same way no model vendor is named in a spec model
(ADR-0002). `mode` is the binding author's statement of intent; the
registry decides the real invocation mode, because a service engine
declared in-process would skip every check that makes the call safe.

`endpoint`, `secret_ref`, `tenant` and `send_data_classes` only mean
anything for an out-of-process engine, where invoking the engine is egress
and is governed exactly like any other external endpoint (ADR-0030).
WorkflowBinding.title: WorkflowBinding

WorkflowInterface.description:
The seam between a governed workflow and a step built elsewhere
(ADR-0110): what goes in and out, what it calls, which data it touches.
The validator checks it as if it were the step.
WorkflowInterface.title: WorkflowInterface

WorkflowSpec.description:
A declarative process graph (see `orgagents.workflows`): a UML
Activity whose nodes are actions calling tools, agents and other
workflows (ADR-0102).

`body: external` says the insides are built in an engine the binding
names; the spec then holds only its `interface` (ADR-0110).
WorkflowSpec.title: WorkflowSpec

WorkingHours.description: When the humans on a channel are actually available.
WorkingHours.title: WorkingHours

description: A System Spec or a Binding in which every element names its UML type as <Profile>::<Name>.
title: OrgAgents typed exchange (ADR-0113)
